parts: Please read /shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/short_families/short_family_reductions.tex, and assess the overall progress of this program, whether it still seems like the most worthwhile program to pursue within quasi-rh-exponent-descent, and whether there are any additional techniques from the repo that could be used to move past the obstacles that have arisen.

I’ll read the short-family reductions alongside the surrounding notes and reviews, then compare the main obstacles with other approaches in the repository. I’ll use that comparison to assess where the program has gained ground and what looks most promising next.

The manuscript has made substantial progress in isolating the problem: the extraction is sharper, the principal term can be removed with suitable profiles, and several error sectors are controlled. The remaining tail estimate is still equivalent to the original short-family moment, however. I’m checking which techniques elsewhere in the repo could supply the missing cancellation, rather than just give another formulation of it.

Short families still looks like the strongest main arithmetic direction in this folder, with mixed-character energy worth keeping in parallel. But every useful target needs more than a quarter-power gain over the generic sieve, so this is a substantial cancellation problem.

Two repo techniques look worth testing: the complete signed covariance method from prime variance, and estimates for the actual coefficient vector from the mixed-family work. A shorter-family parameter range also gives both Möbius factors positive power length across all inner rows; I’m checking whether that creates a useful new point of attack.

I’ll save the assessment as a new review, using the writing skill and the project’s reviews-folder convention. My recommendation is to keep short families primary, but focus the next work on a concrete signed cancellation estimate. The review will also record a checked alternative target: \(h=a=2/5\), which would beat \(7/8\) and gives both Möbius factors positive power length across all inner rows.

**I would keep short families as the main arithmetic direction within quasi-rh-exponent-descent, with mixed-character energy pursued in parallel.** The manuscript makes substantial progress in organizing and narrowing the problem. It has not yet supplied the cancellation needed for a new exponent, and the remaining gap is substantial.

I saved the detailed assessment, including additional calculations and proposed next targets, in [this review](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/reviews/SHORT_FAMILY_PROGRAM_ASSESSMENT_20261008.md). The manuscript is unchanged.

The strongest advances are:

- **Finite extraction from one moment.** Reusing the same fixed-\(h\) hypothesis removes the prime-deletion error without an initial zero-free strip. This materially simplifies what a successful moment theorem must assume. [Extraction theorem](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/short_families/short_family_reductions.tex:271).
- **Principal-term removal without losing zero detection.** The derivative profiles remove the principal density while retaining a detector for every relevant zero away from \(s=1\).
- **An actual negligible-sector estimate.** The adaptive cutoff gives arbitrary power decay for the omitted small-product sector under the complete Schwartz weight. This is stronger than merely identifying a favorable range. [Adaptive theorem](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/short_families/short_family_reductions.tex:663).

These results hold within the manuscript’s explicitly imported arithmetic and Poisson inputs.

The central qualification is that **the remaining adaptive tail moment is equivalent to the original full moment**. The reduction provides better structure, but has not yet weakened the essential cancellation requirement. At \(h=4/5\), the generic sieve supplies the power \(D^{17/15}\), whereas the useful target is \(D^{4/5+a}\), \(a<1/12\). The missing saving is therefore

\[
D^{\,1/3-a},
\qquad 1/3-a>1/4.
\]

That is a substantial arithmetic theorem, not a remaining logarithm or cutoff adjustment. The selected prime-pair component actually inside the tail exhibits this oversized scale, up to logarithms. It does **not** contradict the full target: it establishes that compensation with other factor classes is compulsory. [Tail obstruction](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/short_families/short_family_reductions.tex:1483).

My comparative ranking is:

| Direction | Present role |
|---|---|
| Short families | Strongest developed main arithmetic program |
| Mixed-character energy | Best parallel route to a localized improvement |
| Fixed-scale feedback | Most direct formulation if the objective specifically remains “zeta-only quasi-RH implies RH” |
| Newman collisions | Useful bounded certification project |
| Integer quadratic lift | Lower priority until a new signed correlation mechanism appears |

The distinction in the third row matters. Zeta-only quasi-RH does not automatically provide the new Hecke-family moments. Moreover, \(h_j,a_j\to0\) already approaches RH strength through the single \(u=1\) row. Thus the present program is a route toward stronger arithmetic estimates, rather than an established bootstrap from quasi-RH.

There are several techniques worth bringing across from the repo.

1. **Complete signed covariance and product-coordinate closure.** This is the strongest transfer. The prime-variance work encounters a closely analogous oversized semiprime sector whose cancellation with another sector is necessary. Its product-coordinate identities retain both cutoff edges and the continuum before estimating anything. The algebra extends to ideals:

   \[
   (\mu_K\lambda_u)*(\Lambda_K\lambda_u)
   =-(\mu_K\lambda_u)\log N.
   \]

   Deriving the corresponding complete Eisenstein mixed-discrepancy form could expose cancellation that coefficient norms erase. The analytic remainder and conductor uniformity would need fresh proofs. [Product-coordinate closure](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/prime-variance-exponents/notes/programs/01_signed_arithmetic_covariance/ARITHMETIC_CLOSURE_ATTEMPT_20261004.md:92).

2. **Estimate the actual coefficient vector.** The mixed-family work correctly distinguishes its application’s fixed vector from a stronger arbitrary-vector operator theorem. That distinction is especially valuable here because the manuscript disproves useful estimates for broad selected coefficient classes. Preserve the Möbius coefficients, masks, and coupled factors before applying Cauchy. Its bounded-fiber lemma cannot simply remove the full family’s sixth-power multiplicity. [Mixed-family next target](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/mixed_character_families/notes/2_SELECTED_INVERSE_DISTRIBUTION_20261008.md:454).

3. **Study the compensating cross term explicitly.** Write \(T=U+R\), where \(U\) is the obstructing prime-pair amplitude. Examine
   \[
   \mathcal E(T)=\mathcal E(U)+2\Re\langle U,R\rangle+\mathcal E(R)
   \]
   on radical/core shells. At \(h=4/5\), success requires relative squared-norm suppression exceeding a quarter power. This gives a concrete analytic or numerical diagnostic. The repo already shows why logarithmic anticorrelation, even when real, is insufficient. [Signed covariance precedent](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/prime-variance-exponents/notes/programs/01_signed_arithmetic_covariance/SIGNED_COVARIANCE_CONTINUATION_20261004.md:160).

Root-number coupling is also worth preserving before generic norm bounds, especially for the cube-free convolution coefficients. However, its extra coupling is trivial on the squarefree semiprimes causing the obstruction, so it supplies no immediate cure. [De Faveri, Lemma 3.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.04045v1#S3.SS2).

One additional, checked scout changes the support geometry: take \(h=a=2/5\), \(\theta=1/40\). The target

\[
\mathfrak M(D,D^{2/5})\ll D^{4/5+\varepsilon}
\]

would give \(13/15<7/8\). On every inner row, both Möbius factors then have positive power length:
\[
Nm\ll D^{17/40},\qquad Na,Nb\gg D^{3/40}.
\]
This could suit a signed bilinear attack better than \(h=4/5\). It remains speculative: the generic gap is still \(4/15\), and the full Schwartz family requires shell bookkeeping.

**The next worthwhile milestone is one new signed estimate in an unresolved range.** The repo offers useful methods for preserving and diagnosing the necessary compensation, but I found no existing theorem that already bounds the adaptive tail. Further work should be judged by whether it produces that cancellation, rather than another equivalent reduction.
Please continue with the next milestone

I’ll work toward the signed cancellation estimate by deriving a complete mixed-discrepancy form for the ideal tail and looking for a range where it gives a power saving. I’ll keep the compensating terms together and record exactly what any new bound establishes.

I found an exact cancellation on a family of terms in the tail: grouping every decomposition of a product with two large primes and a small nontrivial cofactor makes the contributions sum to zero.

The balanced semiprime products survive that grouping. Their cancellation must therefore come from different total products, not just from rearranging decompositions of the same product. I’m checking both statements and incorporating them into the mixed-discrepancy calculation.

The cancellation extends to a growing family of small cofactors. It holds on a slightly enlarged row range; the remaining rows are negligible under the Schwartz weight. This gives a controlled sector of the actual signed tail.

I also checked that changing to another fixed detector profile cannot remove the surviving semiprime obstruction to every logarithmic order. The full moment remains open. I’m finishing the reproducible checks and review so the next attempt starts from these sharper results.

The main result now has two clear parts: an exact cancellation removes a family of small-cofactor products, while the surviving semiprime sector forces cancellation across different total products. I’m recording both, with the precise mixed-discrepancy identity for the next analytic step and reproducible checks of the finite algebra.

The separate review found a formula error in the parameter checker: two expressions happened to agree at the chosen test point. I’ve corrected it to the manuscript’s extraction formula and added checks at other parameter values. The mathematical results and the proposed \(13/15\) boundary are unchanged.

The mathematical audits are complete, and all 4,802 finite checks pass with reproducible records. I’m saving the notes, review, and index updates. The manuscript stays unchanged; the next analytic target is the surviving mixed-discrepancy expression with both low/high edges and the cross-product cancellation retained.

Completed the next milestone: **exact signed cancellation in a growing sector of the adaptive tail**.

- [Cancellation result](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/short_families/notes/15_SHORT_FAMILY_DIVISOR_PACKET_CANCELLATION_20261008.md): products with two large primes and a small nonunit cofactor cancel exactly, including nonsquarefree cofactors and deletion masks. Their full weighted energy is negligible.
- [Mixed-discrepancy bridge](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/short_families/notes/14_SHORT_FAMILY_IDEAL_MIXED_DISCREPANCY_20261008.md): connects the tail to the repo’s Möbius–von Mangoldt technique while retaining density, boundaries, and both edge terms.
- [Stronger barrier](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/short_families/notes/16_SHORT_FAMILY_PRODUCT_BARRIER_20261008.md): semiprimes remain oversized after complete productwise recombination for every fixed nonzero profile. Their compensation must cross different total products.

The [review](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/reviews/SHORT_FAMILY_SIGNED_PACKET_REVIEW_20261008.md) records the audits and **4,802 passing finite checks**. Notes and indices are saved; the manuscript is unchanged.

The full moment remains open. The next analytic task is controlling that cross-product compensation through the complete mixed-discrepancy expression.
So has a better bound been found? I see h=2/5 being mentioned but not a mention of a proof

**No better bound for the full short-family moment has been proved.** I should have made that explicit.

The choice \(h=2/5\) is a proposed test point, not a proved improvement. At \(H=D^{2/5}\):

- The existing generic estimate gives \(D^{16/15+\varepsilon}\).
- The proposed target, taking \(a=2/5\), is \(D^{4/5+\varepsilon}\).
- **If that target were proved**, extraction would give the stronger boundary \(13/15\). That remains conditional.

What was proved is narrower: a particular growing family of products cancels exactly, giving negligible weighted energy for that sector. The [proof is in the cancellation note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/short_families/notes/15_SHORT_FAMILY_DIVISOR_PACKET_CANCELLATION_20261008.md). Removing it has **not improved the bound on the remaining tail**.

So this milestone sharpens the reduction and identifies necessary cancellation, but it does not establish a stronger overall moment bound or zero-free strip.
Please write the results about the cancellation into the manuscript before continuing with the investigation

I’ll add the cancellation theorem and its full weighted-sector consequence to the manuscript, with an explicit statement that the full tail bound remains open. Then I’ll compile and review the updated source before returning to the investigation.

The new section includes proofs of the pointwise cancellation and the growing sector’s negligible energy under the full Schwartz weight. It also shows why the two opposing branches can each be large, and identifies the semiprime terms that survive. The \(h=2/5\) choice is explicitly labeled as a sector result, not a proved full-moment bound.

The updated manuscript compiles successfully. Review also clarified a useful distinction: for a fixed prime cofactor, the two selected branches cancel exactly on every row. The complete growing packet sector has the stated negligible weighted bound. Both are now distinguished from the full tail, whose bound remains open.

Added the cancellation results, with complete proofs, to the [manuscript](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/short_families/short_family_reductions.tex:816):

- Exact divisor packet cancellation.
- Negligible energy for the growing sector under the full row weight.
- Large opposing branches and the surviving semiprime obstruction.

The text explicitly states that the full moment bound remains open. Native LaTeX compilation succeeded, and the review and research history are updated.

## My request:
Excellent, now please continue

I’ll continue with the signed cancellation still needed across different total products, using the mixed-discrepancy formulation and keeping both edge terms. The aim is to find a further controlled sector or a stronger bound, with any remaining gap stated explicitly.

Two promising routes have emerged. One gives a block in which composite terms compensate the large prime-pair contribution. The other may let us control the entire nonsquarefree part of the tail by changing the adaptive cutoff. I’m checking the second route’s error bounds; neither result yet bounds the full moment.

The checks support a stronger component result: with cutoff parameter \(\theta=11/20\), the entire nonsquarefree tail has a proved bound \(D^{19/24+\varepsilon}\) at \(H=D^{2/5}\), under the manuscript’s existing analytic inputs. That is below the proposed \(D^{4/5+\varepsilon}\) budget.

This makes nonsquarefree products an affordable error and leaves a squarefree, pairwise-coprime residual. The full moment is still open. I’m writing the proof and checking the row-dependent cutoff step carefully.
Two audits agree with the reduction. I’m checking the algebra and cutoff endpoints, then I’ll save the proof and add it to the manuscript with a clear statement of what remains open.

The proof now has two useful conclusions. At \(H=D^{2/5}\), the nonsquarefree part is below the proposed budget. A separate cofactor argument also identifies a tail block with negligible energy, where cancellation must cross total products. Neither result yet bounds the remaining squarefree sum.

The manuscript addition includes the proof and the reduction to a squarefree residual. The checks also caught two endpoint details: the semiprime coefficient needs \(Y_u\ge1\), and the logarithmic formula must exclude the unit term. Those are corrected; I’m checking compilation now.

The next milestone is proved: using the existing analytic inputs, the **entire nonsquarefree tail** has normalized energy
\[
\ll_\varepsilon D^{19/24+\varepsilon}
\quad\text{at }H=D^{2/5},\ \theta=11/20.
\]
This falls below the proposed \(D^{4/5+\varepsilon}\) budget and rigorously reduces the target to a squarefree signed residual.

**The full moment remains unproved.** Cancellation in that residual is the remaining obstacle.
